title: Finite object and arrow lists lift with relations
statement: Let $J$ be a small filtered category, $F:J\to\mathrm{Cat}$ a diagram of small categories [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], and $O=\operatorname{colim}(F\circ\mathrm{Ob})$ its chosen object-set colimit. Equip $O$ with a category structure and functors $V_j:F(j)\to O$. Assume $V_j$ has the object colimit coprojection as object map and $F(f)\circ V_k=V_j$ for every $f:j\to k$. Assume an arrow-set colimit cocone $a$ and equivalence $e:a.\mathrm{pt}\simeq\mathrm{Arrow}(O)$ identify its coprojections with the arrow maps of $V_j$ [def-weil-pbc-arrows-functor]. For natural numbers $n,m$, lists $X:\mathrm{Fin}(n)\to O$ and $A:\mathrm{Fin}(m)\to\mathrm{Arrow}(O)$ lift to lists $X_j,A_j$ at a single stage $j$, with images exactly $X,A$. Whenever $A_p$ has source (respectively target) $X_q$, $A_{j,p}$ has source (respectively target) $X_{j,q}$. Whenever $A_p,A_q$ have equal middle endpoints and their composite, transported along that endpoint equality, is $A_r$, their stage representatives have equal middle endpoints and composite $A_{j,r}$. Whenever $A_p$ is the identity of $X_q$, $A_{j,p}$ is the identity of $X_{j,q}$.

source.place: proof of Lemma Tag 09YL (lemma-colimit-sites), first paragraph: 'The formula C = colim C_i means that Ob(C) = colim Ob(C_i) and Arrows(C) = colim Arrows(C_i). Then source, target, and composition are inherited ... Remark that given any finite diagram in C there exists an i such that this diagram is the image of a diagram in C_i' (stated without proof); filtered colimits of sets: categories.tex Section Tag 04AX

proof.text:
Choose stage representatives of the objects and arrows using joint
surjectivity of their set colimits. Move the finitely many stages to a common
stage. For each arrow endpoint that equals a listed object in the colimit,
use eventual equality in the object colimit and refine until the equality holds.
Do the same for every pair of arrow endpoints that coincide. At this stage every
listed composite is defined. Functoriality identifies its colimit image with
the listed composite in O. Eventual equality in the arrow colimit now makes
each required composition and identity equation hold at a further stage.
There are finitely many of these equations; a common refinement preserves all
of them. The empty-list case uses the nonemptiness of the filtered category.

lean.statement: theorem filteredColimit_category_finite_lift (J : Type z) [SmallCategory J] [IsFiltered J] (F : J ⥤ Cat.{z, z}) : let O := colimit (F ⋙ Cat.objects) ∀ (_s : Category.{z} O) (V : ∀ j : J, F.obj j ⥤ O), ((∀ (j : J) (X : F.obj j), (V j).obj X = colimit.ι (F ⋙ Cat.objects) j X) ∧ (∀ (j k : J) (f : j ⟶ k), (F.map f).toFunctor ⋙ V k = V j) ∧ (∃ (a : Cocone (F ⋙ Cat.arrows)) (e : a.pt ≃ Arrow O), Nonempty (IsColimit a) ∧ ∀ (j : J) (f : Arrow (F.obj j)), e (a.ι.app j f) = (V j).mapArrow.obj f)) → (∀ (n m : ℕ) (X : Fin n → O) (A : Fin m → Arrow O), ∃ (j : J) (Xj : Fin n → F.obj j) (Aj : Fin m → Arrow (F.obj j)), (∀ q, (V j).obj (Xj q) = X q) ∧ (∀ p, (V j).mapArrow.obj (Aj p) = A p) ∧ (∀ p q, (A p).left = X q → (Aj p).left = Xj q) ∧ (∀ p q, (A p).right = X q → (Aj p).right = Xj q) ∧ (∀ p q r (h : (A p).right = (A q).left), Arrow.mk ((A p).hom ≫ eqToHom h ≫ (A q).hom) = A r → ∃ hj : (Aj p).right = (Aj q).left, Arrow.mk ((Aj p).hom ≫ eqToHom hj ≫ (Aj q).hom) = Aj r) ∧ (∀ p q, A p = Arrow.mk (𝟙 (X q)) → Aj p = Arrow.mk (𝟙 (Xj q))))
